reason: This passage from 1 Kings 19 is substantially narrated from the perspective of Elijah, a prophetic leader. The text explicitly presents Elijah's point of view and captures his complaint about dealing with an ungrateful nation: he describes how the Israelites have abandoned God's covenant (בְרִיתְךָ עָזְבוּ), destroyed the altars (מִזְבְּחֹתֶיךָ הָרָסוּ), killed the prophets with the sword (נְבִיאֶיךָ הָרְגוּ בֶחָרֶב), and now seek his life (וַיְבַקְשׁוּ אֶת־ נַפְשִׁי). Elijah's response to this ingratitude—fleeing into the wilderness and expressing his despair—shows him grappling with the burden of leading a people who have rejected both God and His prophetic messenger.
